newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 higher.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to 0.10 higher.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent a lb firmer Thursday, based on market orders at 1018 EST, dealers said.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture put new sales for the week ended March 20 at 131,400 bales for the 1996/97 crop, lower than market sources had anticipated. pegged exports at 6.8 million bales for the season.
Dealers said the estimate has already been filtered into the market but could support prices at current levels. The expect thin trade ahead of the long Easter weekend.
Merrill Lynch analyst Judith Ganes said the U.S. is on tract to meet the USDA's export target of 6.8 million bales for the current season. Commitments to date reached 5.796 million bales.
Export figures over the next two weeks should be brisk, analysts said, since prices have lingered near recent lows.
Prices closed barely firmer Wednesday, with spot May up 0.06 at 72.65 cents, having ranged from 72.89 to 72.45 cents. Volume was estimated at 11,000 lots.
The USDA will release its planting intentions survey for the new crop Monday at 0830 EST. Analyst pegged the estimate between 13.7 and 14.3 million acres.
The NYCE will be closed Friday for the long Easter weekend.
